## Sketching tangent graphs {#fgt1-tangent .trig-lesson}

For $y=a\tan nx+b$, the period is $T=\dfrac{\pi}{|n|}$.

::: {.split}
::: {.column-block}
<h3>Asymptotes first</h3>

- Mark the centre $(0,b)$.
- Draw the nearest asymptotes at $x=\pm\dfrac{T}{2}$.
- Repeat the asymptotes every $T$ units.

:::
::: {.column-block}
<h3>Then each branch</h3>

- Use $T/4$ to locate guide points.
- Check the direction of the branch.
- Keep the branches separate.

:::
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment}
Tangent has no amplitude. The coefficient $a$ gives a vertical dilation and may also reflect the graph.
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 14 · Example 1.13</p>

::: notes

a,n are nonzero. A tangent graph is unbounded: a vertical dilation factor is not an amplitude. For n>0 the central branch has guide points (−T/4,b−a),(0,b),(T/4,b+a); if n<0 its direction reverses. In general the branch increases when an>0 and decreases when an<0. The unshifted vertical asymptotes are x=(π/2+kπ)/n, k an integer; their spacing is T. Range is R. On a specified domain exclude every asymptote, including boundary values if applicable. This two-minute explanation prepares the next full sketch. Source reference is conceptual; no additional booklet task is assigned here.

:::
